name: Sienna Voss
role: Philanthropist & Heir to the Voss Family Fortune
preparty_markdown:
Sienna is the only member of the Voss dynasty who can attend an arts gala without immediately being asked

for a check, mostly because everyone waits several minutes first. She is stylish, socially fluent, and harder to

read than her public image suggests. She funds young artists, hates being introduced as an heiress, and has

learned to smile through questions about her family.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Composed, witty, guarded, generous when she chooses. You grew up around power and recognize its rituals instantly.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Moves in the same collector circle as Theo Glass and Daphne Palette.

• Has commissioned work from Imogen Muse.

• Beatrice Plinth has known Sienna since childhood and refuses to be impressed by her surname.

COSTUME

Modern gala glamour: elegant cocktail dress or formal suit, statement jewelry, designer-looking clutch, effortless rather than

ostentatious.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Yes, that Voss. No, I do not know what the stock is doing.”

“Philanthropy is when your family argument gets a plaque.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Everett Locke
role: Director of Museum Security & Former Art-Crimes Investigator
preparty_markdown:
Everett spent years investigating stolen art before discovering that museums contain nearly as much intrigue

with better climate control. He is calm, observant, and difficult to surprise. He notices open doors, blocked

sight lines, unattended bags, and people who suddenly become interested in exits. Tonight he would prefer

everyone simply enjoy the exhibition, which means they almost certainly will not.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Low-key, skeptical, dry, watchful. Ask where people were and remember their answers.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Coordinates closely with Adrian Vellum and Rafael Gilt.

• Frequently clashes with Nadia Quill over access and with Juno March over protest tactics.

• Riley Bloom keeps changing layouts after Everett has already approved them.

COSTUME

Dark suit, discreet earpiece prop if desired, security-style watch, small notebook. Do not dress as a cop; think senior

museum security professional.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Nothing ruins ambience like an incident report.”

“If you moved it, tell me now. If you did not move it, tell me who did.”

name: Nadia Quill
preparty_markdown:
Nadia covers the art world the way other reporters cover city hall: money, power, access, and who benefits

when everyone agrees not to ask a question. Her pieces are sharp, deeply sourced, and occasionally followed

by nervous legal letters. She has been invited tonight because excluding her would look worse.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Curious, direct, quick, socially fearless. Ask questions people wish you would save for email.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Professional rival of Morgan Slate, whose criticism Nadia considers entertaining but insufficiently documented.

• Avery Lens has photographed several of Nadia's stories.

• Helena Cross has threatened to quote Nadia's own articles back to her in court.

COSTUME

Cocktail attire with practical reporter touches: blazer, notebook, pen, compact camera if desired. Stylish enough for the gala,

ready enough for a press scrum.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Off the record is not a magic spell.”

“If three people call something a misunderstanding, I start taking notes.”
